messages.content: The return has now been changed to Thursday morning, so I need the Baltimore hotel for three nights: Monday, August 18 through Thursday, August 21. Please compare the full cost of the two properties we discussed, including breakfast, and tell me how I would get to the Walters for the 7:30 a.m. call.

I have both available for all three nights. Hotel Revival is $214 per night, with $96.30 in taxes and fees, for a room total of $738.30. Breakfast is not included; the hotel’s breakfast menu runs about $18 to $24 per person before tax and tip. It is about a 10-minute walk to the Walters, so leaving around 7:15 a.m. should be sufficient.

The Midtown Plaza is $176 per night plus $79.20 in taxes and fees, totaling $607.20. Breakfast is included. It is not comfortably walkable with work materials; the practical route is the Purple Route circulator or a short rideshare. For a 7:30 call, I would leave by 6:55 for transit or about 7:05 by rideshare. Its refundable rate must be canceled by 6:00 p.m. on August 14, while Hotel Revival remains refundable until 6:00 p.m. on August 17.
What does Revival come to if my wife has breakfast with me Tuesday and Wednesday, but I leave too early to eat there Thursday?

Using $21 per person as a reasonable midpoint, four breakfasts add $84 before tax and tip. Allowing roughly $101 total with tax and a 20% tip, Hotel Revival would come to about $839.30 for the stay and those breakfasts. The exact meal total would depend on what you order.
So the difference is about $232 compared with Midtown Plaza, and Midtown includes breakfast for both of us?

Yes. On the current quotes, Midtown Plaza is about $232.10 less overall. Its included breakfast covers both registered guests Tuesday and Wednesday; Thursday breakfast begins at 7:00 a.m., which is unlikely to work with your morning flight.
How dependable is that circulator early Tuesday? I cannot be late for the museum call.

The published weekday service begins early enough, but frequency and downtown traffic make it less predictable than walking. The stop is about three minutes from the hotel, followed by a roughly 9-minute ride and a 4-minute walk. I would plan for the 6:58 departure, with the 7:10 run as a narrow fallback. A rideshare is typically 6 to 10 minutes door to door and would be the more dependable choice that morning.
Price out one rideshare Tuesday morning and walking on Wednesday. Wednesday does not start until 9:00.

A Tuesday morning rideshare is currently estimated at $11 to $16. Wednesday’s walk is about 18 minutes on a straightforward route, so leaving at 8:35 would provide a small buffer. Even using the high end of the rideshare estimate, Midtown Plaza would remain about $216 less than Revival.
That settles the location question. Before you book, what room types are actually available at Midtown?

The refundable rate is available in a room with one king bed at $176 per night and a room with two queen beds at $184 per night. The two-queen room raises the three-night total, including taxes and fees, to $633.96. Both room types include breakfast for two and Wednesday luggage storage after checkout is not relevant now because you are staying through Thursday morning.
For this Baltimore trip, book the two-queen room. My wife and I want separate beds this time because I will be getting up well before her on Thursday.

The two-queen refundable room is selected for Monday, August 18 through Thursday, August 21. The total is $633.96, breakfast for two is included, and cancellation is permitted until 6:00 p.m. local time on Thursday, August 14. Shall I complete it using project code BAL-DEINST-820?
Yes. Put the room on that project code, but note that her breakfasts and any other personal charges must stay off the museum expense report.

Booked Midtown Plaza Baltimore for three nights, checking in Monday, August 18 and checking out Thursday, August 21. The reservation is for two guests in one room with two queen beds at a total lodging charge of $633.96 under project code BAL-DEINST-820. Breakfast for two is included; personal incidental charges are to be kept separate from the museum folio. Free cancellation ends at 6:00 p.m. local time on August 14. Hotel confirmation: MPB-481726. For Tuesday’s 7:30 a.m. museum call, plan on a rideshare around 7:05; Wednesday’s 9:00 a.m. call is an approximately 18-minute walk, leaving around 8:35.
